372498.title: Exponential non-isomorphism conjecture for spanning trees of regular graphs
372498.statement:
Let $n,d\geq 3$ be integers, and let $G$ be a connected $n$-vertex $d$-regular graph. Write $T_{\mathrm{unlabeled}}(G)$ for the set of isomorphism classes of spanning trees of $G$. **Exponential spanning-tree conjecture.** There exists a universal constant $c>0$ depending only on $d$ such that

$$
|T_{\mathrm{unlabeled}}(G)|\geq e^{cn}.
$$

The paper proves an analogous result for sufficiently large degree and asks whether the threshold can be reduced to $d_0=3$; the conjecture asserts this bound for every $d\geq3$.

372499.title: Exponential anticoncentration conjecture for random spanning trees
372499.statement:
Let $\varepsilon>0$ be real. There is a constant $d_{\varepsilon}>0$ such that for every integer $d\geq d_{\varepsilon}$, every connected $n$-vertex $d$-regular graph $G$, and a uniformly random spanning tree $\mathcal{T}$ of $G$, let $T$ be any $n$-vertex tree. **Optimal anticoncentration conjecture.**

$$
\Pr\bigl[\mathcal{T}\simeq_{\mathrm{iso}}T\bigr]\leq e^{-(1-\varepsilon)n}.
$$

The conjecture is motivated by the expected number of copies of a fixed tree in a random graph and is supported for the path by the Brégman–Minc inequality. The stated exponential scale is best possible up to lower-order terms, while extension to suitable $(n,d,\lambda)$-graphs is posed as an additional direction.

372532.title: The topological exactness conjecture for hard telic problems
372532.statement:
Let $(X,T)$ be an efficiently discretizable topological dynamical system. Recall that $T$ is **topologically exact** if, for every nonempty open set $U\subset X$, there exists $n_0\in\mathbb{N}$ such that $T^{n_0}(U)=X$. A telic problem is called hard-on-average when it satisfies the stated almost-everywhere average-case hardness condition.

**Topological exactness conjecture.** If $T$ is topologically exact and the system admits a hard telic problem, then there exists an almost-everywhere $\delta$ hard-on-average telic problem coming from the dynamical system.

The conjecture is motivated by the possible construction of one-way functions from dynamical systems with hard telic problems. Its resolution is not supplied in the source.

372549.title: The conjecture on the possible numbers of one-element commutation classes
372549.statement:
Let $n\geq 1$ and let $\sigma\in\mathfrak{S}_{n+1}$. Let $R_{\bullet}(\sigma)$ denote the set of one-element commutation classes of reduced words of $\sigma$. **The possible-cardinalities conjecture.** For all $\sigma\in\mathfrak{S}_{n+1}$,

$$
|R_{\bullet}(\sigma)|\in\{0,1,2,4\}.
$$

Theorem 7.1 gives the upper bound $|R_{\bullet}(\sigma)|\leq 4$, while computation through $n=8$ found no example with exactly three one-element commutation classes. The conjecture asserts that three never occurs; the source does not report a proof or disproof.

372593.title: Positivity conjecture for the plane-partition D'Arcais differences
372593.statement:
Let $\sigma_2(n):=\sum_{d\mid n}d^2$, and let $\Delta_n^{\sigma_2}(x)$ denote the difference associated with the D'Arcais polynomials for $g(n)=\sigma_2(n)$. **Plane-partition positivity conjecture.** For every $n\in\mathbb{N}$,

$$
\Delta_n^{\sigma_2}(x)>0\quad\text{for }x\geq g(2)=5,
$$

and, moreover, for every $n\geq 6$,

$$
\Delta_n^{\sigma_2}(x)>0\quad\text{for }x\geq 1.
$$

The claim is motivated by the computed values and plots in the paper; the supplied material gives no resolution, so its status remains open.

372616.title: Duality conjecture for normed flow indices
372616.statement:
Let $G$ be a bridgeless graph and let $d\ge 2$ be an integer. For $p\in[1,2]$ and $q\in[2,\infty]$, write $\phi_{d,p}(G)$ and $\phi_{d,q}(G)$ for the corresponding flow indices. **Duality conjecture for normed flow indices.** For every $p\in[1,2]$, there exists $q\in[2,\infty]$ such that

$$
\phi_{d,p}(G)=\phi_{d,q}(G),
$$

and conversely, for every $q\in[2,\infty]$, there exists $p\in[1,2]$ satisfying the same equality. The source contrasts this with the usual duality relation $1/p+1/q=1$ and leaves the asserted existence open.

372618.title: The generalized $S^2_p$-flow conjecture
372618.statement:
For a bridgeless graph $G$, let

$$
S_p^{d-1}:=\{\boldsymbol{x}\in\mathbb{R}^d:\lVert\boldsymbol{x}\rVert_p=1\}
$$

be the unit $p$-sphere. **The generalized $S^2_p$-flow conjecture.** For every bridgeless graph $G$ and every $p\in[1,\infty]$,

$$
\phi_{3,p}(G)=2.
$$

This extends Jain's $S^2$-flow conjecture from the Euclidean sphere to all $p$-norms. The source notes that the case $p=\infty$ is proved, while the general assertion is suggested using the preceding monotonicity and duality conjectures.

372630.title: Extremal Sylow 2-subgroups conjecture for even-cycle-intersecting families
372630.statement: Let $S_n$ be the symmetric group on $n$ elements. A family of permutations is **even-cycle-intersecting** when every pair of permutations has a common cycle of even length in the relevant intersection condition. A Sylow $2$-subgroup of $S_n$ is a maximal subgroup whose order is a power of $2$, and a double-translate is a family obtained by multiplying such a subgroup on the left and right by fixed permutations. **Extremal Sylow 2-subgroups conjecture.** For every $n\geq 2$, the extremal even-cycle-intersecting families of $S_n$ are the Sylow $2$-subgroups and their double-translates. This conjecture identifies the proposed extremal families, but the supplied text gives no resolution beyond stating it as future work.

372631.title: Extremal Sylow p-subgroups conjecture for p-singular families of general linear groups
372631.statement: Let $p\in\mathbb{N}$ be prime, let $q$ be a power of $p$, and let $\mathrm{GL}_{n,q}$ denote the general linear group over the field with $q$ elements. A family is **$p$-singular** if its elements have order divisible by $p$. A Sylow $p$-subgroup is a subgroup of maximal order among the $p$-subgroups, and a double-translate is obtained by multiplying it on the left and right by fixed elements of $\mathrm{GL}_{n,q}$. **Extremal Sylow $p$-subgroups conjecture.** For all $n\geq 2$, the Sylow $p$-subgroups and their double-translates are the extremal $p$-singular families of $\mathrm{GL}_{n,q}$. The conjecture proposes the analogue of the symmetric-group extremal result for finite general linear groups; the supplied text gives no resolution.

372634.title: Linear non-separating independent-set conjecture for link-diagram dual graphs
372634.statement: Let $D$ be a reduced link diagram with $n$ crossings, and let $\Gamma(D)$ be its dual graph. An independent set in $\Gamma(D)$ is **non-separating** if deleting its vertices does not disconnect $\Gamma(D)$. **Non-separating independent-set conjecture.** There exists a constant $\delta>0$ such that, for every reduced link diagram $D$ with $n$ crossings, $\Gamma(D)$ contains a non-separating independent set of size at least $\delta n$. This is the graph-theoretic formulation proposed as equivalent to the conjectured improvement of the three-page-index bound; the source leaves its proof for future work and gives no resolution.

372658.title: Near-optimal spectral-gap meta-conjecture for random hyperbolic surfaces
372658.statement:
Let $(X_k)_k$ be a sequence of random finite-area hyperbolic surfaces such that

$$
\lim_{k\to\infty}\operatorname{Vol}(X_k)=+\infty.
$$

Write $\lambda_1(X_k)$ for the first positive Laplace eigenvalue. **Random hyperbolic-surface spectral-gap meta-conjecture.** For every $\epsilon>0$,

$$
\lim_{k\to+\infty}\mathbb{P}\left(\lambda_1(X_k)\geq\frac14-\epsilon\right)=1.
$$

The claim predicts that random hyperbolic surfaces asymptotically achieve the universal-cover threshold $1/4$ with high probability. It is presented as a meta-conjecture motivated by the analogy with random regular graphs and Selberg's conjecture; the source does not give a resolution.

372663.title: Biedl's logarithmic basis number conjecture
372663.statement:
Let $G$ be an $n$-vertex graph, and let $\operatorname{bn}(G)$ denote the basis number of $G$. **Biedl's logarithmic basis number conjecture.** Every $n$-vertex graph $G$ has

$$
\operatorname{bn}(G)\in O(\log n).
$$

The conjecture proposes a logarithmic upper bound on the basis number for arbitrary graphs. The source presents it as an unresolved conjecture and attributes it to Biedl; it suggests that insights from the paper's proof may help establish it.

372684.title: Infinite admissible lengths conjecture for consecutive prime sums
372684.statement:
Let $p_n$ denote a prime number, and for each integer $k\geq 1$ define

$$
S_k(p_n)=p_n+p_{n+1}+\cdots+p_{n+k-1},
$$

where $p_{n+i}$ are consecutive primes. **Infinite admissible lengths conjecture.** For every prime number $p_n$, there exist infinitely many odd integers $k\geq 3$ such that

$$
S_k(p_n)
$$

is a prime number. This strengthens the existence conjecture by asserting recurrence rather than merely one admissible length; the source supports it with numerical evidence and heuristic probabilistic arguments, but gives no proof.

372693.title: Degeneracy conjecture for proper conflict-free degree-plus list coloring
372693.statement: A graph $G$ is **$d$-degenerate** if every subgraph of $G$ has a vertex of degree at most $d$. For a graph $G$, a $({\rm degree}+d)$-list assignment assigns each vertex $v$ a list $L(v)$ with $|L(v)|\geq d_G(v)+d$. A graph is proper conflict-free $({\rm degree}+d)$-choosable if it has a proper conflict-free $L$-coloring for every such list assignment. **Degeneracy conjecture.** If a connected graph $G\ne C_5$ is $d$-degenerate for some positive integer $d$, then $G$ is proper conflict-free $({\rm degree}+d)$-choosable. The paper proves the corresponding bound with $d+1$ in place of $d$; reducing it by one is presented as challenging and remains open.

372705.title: The invariant-set conjecture for random graph edge perturbations
372705.statement:
A sequence $\textbf{p}\in(0,1)^\omega$ is Borel–Cantelli, and a graph $G=(\omega,E_G)$ is $\textbf{p}$-random. Write $[\omega]^2$ for the set of two-element subsets of $\omega$.

**Invariant-set conjecture.** For any Borel–Cantelli sequence $\textbf{p}$ and $\textbf{p}$-random graph $G=(\omega,E_G)$, there exists an infinite set $A\subseteq[\omega]^2$ such that, for every $B\subseteq A$, the graph

$$
\left(\omega,\left(E_G\setminus A\right)\cup B\right)
$$

is isomorphic to $G$.

This conjecture is introduced as a way to organize drawable graphs and is abbreviated in the source as $\operatorname{ISC}$. Its status is not resolved in the supplied text.

372706.title: The sparsifying-transduction characterization of dense class properties
372706.statement:
Let $\mathscr C$ be a class of TOWS graphs, and let $\mathsf{Sp}(\mathscr C)$ be the class obtained by the paper's sparsifying transduction. Let $\Pi_S$ be a downset of weakly sparse class properties: if $\mathscr C\in\Pi_S$ and $\mathscr D$ is a weakly sparse transduction of $\mathscr C$, then $\mathscr D\in\Pi_S$. Define the dense analogue $\Pi$ by requiring every weakly sparse transduction of $\mathscr C$ to belong to $\Pi_S$. **Sparsifying-transduction conjecture.** For every class $\mathscr C$ of TOWS graphs,

$$
\mathscr C\in\Pi\qquad\iff\qquad\mathsf{Sp}(\mathscr C)\in\Pi_S.
$$

This would transfer every downclosed weakly sparse class property to its dense analogue through $\mathsf{Sp}$; the supplied text gives no resolution status.

372713.title: Weyl-algebra subalgebra graph-admissibility conjecture
372713.statement: Let $A_n$ be the complex $n$-mode Weyl algebra, and let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a finite-dimensional Lie subalgebra of $A_n$. **Weyl-algebra subalgebra conjecture.** Every finite-dimensional Lie subalgebra of $A_n$ is graph-admissible but not necessarily minimal-graph-admissible. This asks whether graph-admissibility persists for finite-dimensional subalgebras in higher-mode Weyl algebras, while minimal graph-admissibility may fail.

372744.title: Permutation conjecture for modular-polynomial evaluations outside the invariant image
372744.statement:
Let $N$ be the level parameter, let $\alpha$ be the invariant, let $\operatorname{image}\alpha$ denote its image, let $\Phi_m^{\alpha}$ be the modular polynomial with level structure, and let $\psi(m)$ be the degree parameter appearing in the construction. **Permutation conjecture.** For any positive integer $m$ prime to $N$, there exists a permutation $\sigma$ on $\mathbb{C}\setminus\operatorname{image}\alpha$ such that

$$
\Phi_m^{\alpha}(z,Y)=(Y-\sigma(z))^{\psi(m)},
$$

for every $z\in\mathbb{C}\setminus\operatorname{image}\alpha$. This conjecture describes the evaluation of the modular polynomials at points outside the image of the invariant, where all roots coincide according to a permutation of the complement.

372759.title: Extension conjecture for type B parking-space representations
372759.statement:
Let $B_n$ be the signed symmetric group on $n$ letters, with inclusion $B_n\subset B_{n+1}$ given by choosing the elements of $B_{n+1}$ that fix the $(n+1)$st letter. For $m,n\geq 1$, let $\mathbb{C}[(\mathbb{Z}/m\mathbb{Z})^n]$ be the corresponding $B_n$-representation. **Extension conjecture.** For all $m,n\geq 1$, there exists a representation $V_{n,m}$ of $B_{n+1}$ such that

$$
\operatorname{Res}^{B_{n+1}}_{B_n}V_{n,m}\cong \mathbb{C}[(\mathbb{Z}/m\mathbb{Z})^n].
$$

This generalizes the extension question for the type $B$ parking space, which is the representation $\mathbb{C}[(\mathbb{Z}/(2n+1)\mathbb{Z})^n]$. The source presents this as its main conjecture; no resolution is given here.

372796.title: The bounded perfect derived subgroup conjecture for pointwise stabilizers
372796.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite primitive group acting on a set, and consider the pointwise stabilizer $H$ of two points in this action. 

**Bounded perfect derived subgroup conjecture.** There exists an absolute constant $c$ such that $H^{(c)}$ is perfect.

This conjecture generalizes the known result for primitive groups with solvable stabilizer, where two points can be chosen so that their pointwise stabilizer has derived length bounded by an absolute constant. The preceding theorem establishes a uniform bound for the derived subgroups of stabilizers in primitive perfect groups, but the stated assertion for all finite primitive groups remains open.
